author: 5kO0
content:
Implemented (this session). Added 7 property tests in proto-blue-repo/tests/property_tests.rs and 1 fuzz target in fuzz/fuzz_targets/proof_construct_verify.rs.

Property tests:
  1. proof_verifies_present_key      — soundness: covering_proof verifies actual value for present keys
  2. proof_rejects_wrong_value       — completeness: wrong-value claim must not verify
  3. proof_verifies_absence_for_missing_key — absence proofs work for non-members
  4. block_removal_never_produces_silent_false_accept — strict-superset / overestimate property: removing any block from a valid proof either (a) still verifies (block was redundant) or (b) returns MissingBlock. Never Ok(false). This is the tranquil-pds invariant.
  5. extra_blocks_do_not_change_verdict — verifier ignores unrelated noise blocks
  6. tamper_cannot_force_wrong_value_acceptance — forgery resistance: no proof-byte mutation combined with a wrong-value claim can produce Ok(true)
  7. covering_proof_is_superset_of_each_directional_proof — structural: covering = key ∪ left-sibling ∪ right-sibling

Fuzz target (proof_construct_verify):
  Builds an MST from arbitrary fuzzer-driven (key, value) data, generates covering_proof, exercises verifier on clean + adversarially-mutated copies. Mutations: drop a block, flip a byte, add an unrelated block. Asserts (a) no panic on any input, (b) no silent acceptance of forged-value claims regardless of mutation.

Notable finding during property-test development: my initial byte_tamper test asserted "any byte tamper breaks verification of the queried key." That failed on a 2-entry MST where the tamper landed in the OTHER entry's value-CID encoding, which the lookup path for the queried key never consults. The verifier correctly returned Ok(true) for the still-true original claim — no forgery occurred. I rewrote the test as forgery-resistance (tamper + wrong-value claim must never yield Ok(true)), which is the actual security property and what the verifier's contract promises. The "every byte tamper must break something" property would only hold if lookup_in_proof did CID-consistency checking on every block it consulted — that's a separate hardening that belongs upstream (CAR reader, MstNode::load) and is already present there.

Verification (rust-quality §honest reporting):
  cargo build -p proto-blue-repo --tests   PASS
  cargo build --workspace                  PASS
  cargo build --bin proof_construct_verify PASS
  cargo test -p proto-blue-repo            PASS (13 property tests + all unit + 2 doctests; no failures)
  cargo clippy -p proto-blue-repo --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings  PASS
  cargo clippy --bin proof_construct_verify -- -D warnings  PASS
  cargo fmt -p proto-blue-repo --check     PASS
  cargo fmt (in fuzz/)                     PASS (after applying)
  cargo +nightly fuzz run proof_construct_verify -- -runs=1000  PASS (no crashes; corpus grew to 32 inputs / 1320 covered code points / 2668 features)

Behavioural change: none (test-only code; no production source modified). The audit's predicted bug class (silent acceptance of insufficient-blocks proofs) was NOT surfaced — proto-blue's verifier correctly returns Err(MissingBlock) under all the deletion mutations the tests exercised.

Category: A (root-cause) — added the entire missing test category, not a single-site patch.
